motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: Edge draw and the travelling dot.

motion.name: ripple

motion.name: glide
motion.purpose: Camera to a focused module, a picked change, or back to the whole atlas.

motion.name: panel
motion.purpose: Detail panel and its backing strip, when the reader opens or closes it.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Dimming and lighting of cards and edges.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: drag, scroll, click or any key but left/right
motion.purpose: Jumps the ripple to its end state.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes the ripple, the walk, the glides, the panel slide and all transitions.

motion.name: walk
motion.value: lead 560ms to the trigger at 0.85 zoom; each edge 300ms; 140ms pause per step, 560ms more at a change

narrative.overview:
The viewer is an agent-builder canvas: white cards on a light grey field, joined by thin lines that turn at right angles, read left to right. The look follows OpenAI Agent Builder's canvas, which the user pinned. Nothing on the field is decorative. A card shows what kind of step it is, its name, and the change it carries when it has one; a branch is named on its line. All chrome floats over the canvas: a headline block top left and a panel on the right. None of it is docked into columns.

The whole product is one map, fitted across the available desktop width at a readable layout density. Its height never reduces the overview zoom: long maps continue vertically and are reached by panning. Each module is grouped by its title and spacing, with its flows directly on the canvas. A flow this change touches is drawn cut down to the change, left to right: the steps it touches, the step each of them is reached from, and where the flow starts; a dotted line stands for whatever lies between and says how many steps it leaves out ("中间 6 步"). A step the change leaves alone is a small pill, a step it touches is a card that says what changed in plain words with its test status, and the three things a change can do to a step read apart at a glance (added: green, a plus at the corner; removed: red and dashed, a minus; altered: amber, a pencil). Branches are named on their lines, every line turns at right angles, and a flow too long for the width wraps onto a second band. A flow the change leaves alone is one row with its name and step count; when changed code is on its way, the row says how many changes instead ("11 处改动会经过这里"). Each flow names what starts it (a request, a background task, a schedule) beside its name, so no line has to cross the map to say so. Every module group keeps to one grid: a touched module runs the full width, changes outside the flows share a strip under it, and the untouched modules share rows of equal cells, all on the same left and right edge. The headline block says where the change lands and what needs attention, and steps through the changes one at a time ("1 / 6", or ← →); the picked card rings, the rest quiet, its details open on the right, and its local flow is highlighted. Cross-module relations and their toggle are removed. Clicking a module heading or a row opens that module in place: every step of its flows is drawn, the cards slide to their new places, and the rest dims; the same native ghost Button in the heading closes it again. With no report to walk, "走一遍" walks a drawn flow where it stands (opening the module first for a flow still shown as a row) from its trigger to its end under a status bar that names the flow, the step reached and a way to stop. Nothing switches pages, and there is no list beside the map: the changes are written on it.

Three signal colours do all the talking. Amber marks change and what it reaches, red marks risk and loss, and blue marks selection. Everything else is ink on white or grey. The density suits reading at a desk: 18px headline, 14px cards, 12 to 12.5px secondary text, and generous space between ranks.

This world replaces the earlier ticket-wallet world. Stamps, perforations, condensed display type and navy carrier colour belong to that world and are gone. The pan-and-zoom canvas it refused is now the primary surface.

Module groups have no enclosing background, border, radius, shadow or padding. A 48px header and 64px gap separate them on the canvas. Desktop overview and module framing use the available width alone, clamped between zoom 0.05 and 1.6. The 0.8 value controls layout density, not a camera floor. Map height and browser height do not reduce that zoom; long maps continue vertically below the viewport.

The camera reserves the free area below the measured headline with 24px separation, left of the open inspector (its width plus 40px), and above a 24px desktop bottom margin. Automatic overview and module zoom use only that area’s width, growing small maps up to 1.6. Opening details fits the same atlas or focused module across the remaining width, without magnifying a single step or shrinking the entire map to its height. If the selected step is below the visible area, the camera pans vertically to reveal it at that width-derived zoom. Closing details restores the wider top-aligned overview or module; resizing recalculates the width fit. Long diagrams remain vertically pannable.

Zooming out retains the normal card surfaces, labels and tone borders. No opaque far-view blocks cover changed cards or changes off the map, and low zoom alone does not fade the other cards. The separate analysis-status pill and cross-module relations toggle are removed.
keyCharacteristics: Light grey canvas (#f4f4f5) with white cards, 18px corners, a hairline border and a soft two-layer shadow.
Pastel kind tiles (trigger green, action violet, decision orange, external yellow, result grey) are the only colour at rest.
Amber is change and what it reaches; red is risk and removal; blue is selection.
Floating chrome only: the headline block top left, the details panel on the right, zoom controls at the bottom right. The map itself carries the changes; nothing lists them beside it.
One light rendition and system sans throughout. Mono is used only for code, paths, revisions and flows still named after their code.
Motion explains the change and nothing else: one ripple of at most 0.6s, a camera glide between changes of one flow, no entrance.
Header-only module groups place flows directly on the canvas. Desktop framing fits the available width, while long diagrams extend vertically and remain pannable.

rules.name: The Three Signals Rule
rules.body: Amber means change and what it reaches, red means risk or what a change removed, and blue means selection. No other element may use these hues, and none of them may appear as decoration.

rules.name: The Change-Is-Amber Rule
rules.body: Every change on the map carries an amber field and a 45% amber border, and only changes do. The change the reader picks takes the solid border and halo, and the steps it leads to answer in amber.

rules.name: The No-Bold Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and ink tone, with weights capped at 500. Text is never uppercase or letterspaced.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Code Rule
rules.body: Monospace is only for code, file paths, test ids and revisions. Flows and steps still named after their code use it because their names are raw identifiers.

rules.name: The Quiet-Around-The-Change Rule
rules.body: When a change is on show, every card but the change, the steps it leads to (once the ripple reaches them) and a card opened in the panel drops its shadow, turns 75% white, fades its content to 60% and takes a grayscale tile. Edges outside the ripple, the way in and the change's own loops fall to 45%, their labels to 60%. A change off the map quiets the whole flow behind it. Quiet cards stay legible. They are never hidden.

dos: **Do** write the change on the card it touches, as a field inside the card.
**Do** keep amber for change: the changed cards, the one picked, the lines to what it touches.
**Do** keep red to risk and removal, and blue to selection.
**Do** float every piece of chrome over the canvas with the float shadow and a hairline ring, 12px from the edge.
**Do** quiet cards around the change (no shadow, grayscale tile, faded content) instead of hiding them.
**Do** give every step kind its pastel tile and Lucide glyph, at 32px on cards and 28px on pills and in the panel.
**Do** stack before above after in the panel so both can be read at a glance.
**Do** let only what changes move: the sentence fades, the flow prefix stays.
donts: **Don't** split the product into pages; it is one map, a module opens in place, and stepping through the changes only moves the camera.
**Don't** dock columns beside the canvas or list the changes beside the map: they are written on it, and details live in the one panel, one subject at a time.
**Don't** add a navigator, a second counter or a change list; the headline walks the changes.
**Don't** add an entrance animation or a canvas fade-in.
**Don't** use stamps, perforations, condensed display faces, uppercase labels or letterspacing.
**Don't** add a dark rendition or tinted card backgrounds. Cards are white and the canvas is #f4f4f5.
**Don't** use bold type. Hierarchy stops at 500.
**Don't** imply a test ran. Statuses say what reading the code found and never claim more.
**Don't** add a footer, a byline or a provenance line; the canvas runs to the bottom edge.

**Don't** shrink the overview or an open module to fit the page height. Fit the available desktop width and let long maps extend vertically; 0.8 is layout density, not a camera floor. Unchanged synthesized flows are diagrams too.
**Don't** add enclosing module cards or cross-module relation lines, share one lane between several lines, or place a group off the grid: every group ends on the same left and right edge.
